full_judgment: 4. On the other hand, Mr Mahmudul Islam along with Dr AKM Ali, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2, The Securities and Exchange Commission, by filing counter-affidavit, submits that the petitioner earlier came before this Court while cognizance of the offence was taken by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and the Sessions Judge by a judgment and order dated 1-6-1997 held that the Criminal Revision Case against the petitioner is liable to be quashed but he has no jurisdiction to quash or to make a reference to the High Court Division under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with his recommendation to quash the said proceeding. The High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 9-12-1997 passed in Criminal Reference No.3 of 1997 rejected the reference. Thereafter the petitioner moved before the Appellate Division and filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.54 of 1998 which was dismissed on 13-5-1998. The said judgment of the Appellate Division was reported in 50 DLR (AD) 189. The Metropolitan Magistrate took cognizance of the offence under section 25 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 and the charge was framed on the allegation as contained in the petition of complaint which was supported by an inquiry report under section 21 of the said Ordinance. The inquiry report has been made part of the complaint and the Appellate Division in the case of Shinepukur Holdings Ltd vs Securities and Exchange Commission reported in 50 DLR (AD) 189 in para 16 held that there is prima facie allegation of contravention of section 17 of the Ordinance in the complaint petition and, as such, the proceeding cannot be quashed at this stage. Further, he submits that the petitioner's act of trading at the relevant point of time was not normal. The inquiry committee detected certain irregularities, which is indicative of manipulative trading by the petitioner and, as such, without taking further evidence and deposition during the trial the genuineness of the allegation as contemplated in the petition of complaint cannot be established. He further submits that the petitioner acted on the basis of unsigned order given by Satkhira Fisheries for the sale of shares of Shinepukur Holdings Limited which cannot be seen as an isolated action. On the face of it, an unsigned order would make the order itself void and action on the basis of such an order is indication of manipulative trading which would constitute an offence under the Ordinance and, as such, in case of unsigned order the presumption would be that such an order is false order. Therefore, the charge on the allegation of false order has rightly been framed. The person in charge of the concerned officers of the department during the period of occurrence of the offence has gone into retirement and that the officers now responsible for the concerned department have been named as witness and the trial Court has considered the material on record and applied judicial mind in framing the charge and unless and until the evidences taken, the proceeding at this stage cannot be quashed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. By referring 55 DLR (AD) 47. Mr Mahmudul Islam submits that the proceeding of the actual case cannot be found if the inquiry report was not filed. Thereby the Appellate Division found that the prosecution has made out prima facie case against the accused and they acted against provision of the Ordinance. Therefore, the proceeding cannot be quashed.
